project.name: TableStory Recipe App Rebrand
project.summary: Convert Pocket Cinema into a coherent recipe discovery product for mobile and television.
project.problem: The reusable application capabilities are hidden behind a film-domain model, terminology, and visual identity that do not serve home cooks.
project.desired_outcome: A reviewer can discover, inspect, and save recipes on mobile or by TV remote without encountering cinema-domain language.

users.need: Find a suitable recipe and understand what it requires.
Read and navigate recipes from a television without a pointer.
Review an observable transformation with objective evidence.

requirements.statement: Every supported surface uses the TableStory brand, recipe terminology, and accessible warm visual system.
requirements.success_evidence: Rendered pages and automated terminology checks contain no prohibited cinema language.

requirements.statement: The app exposes deterministic recipe data, recipe-domain APIs, search semantics, and cookbook persistence in memory.
requirements.source: Recipe content model; Functional requirements 3, 5, and 6
requirements.success_evidence: API tests verify 12 recipes, search, lookup, rails, and cookbook add/remove behavior.

requirements.statement: Mobile users can browse, search, open, understand, save, and remove recipes at 375 CSS pixels.
requirements.success_evidence: A browser test completes the mobile browse-to-detail-to-cookbook journey without horizontal scrolling.

requirements.statement: TV users can browse named rails, open a recipe, operate cookbook and back actions using only remote-equivalent keys.
requirements.success_evidence: Automated keyboard tests open a recipe in mode=tv, use Escape and Backspace to return, preserve mode=tv, and restore visible focus to the originating card.

requirements.statement: Documentation and automated checks prove the rebrand is complete and locally reproducible.
requirements.success_evidence: README startup instructions work and all configured gates pass from a clean checkout.

journeys.name: Find and save dinner
journeys.outcome: A home cook finds a dish by ingredient and saves it to My Cookbook.

journeys.name: Cook from the television
journeys.outcome: A kitchen viewer reaches a recipe and returns to the same TV rail and card using only remote-equivalent keys.
steps: Return to TV browse with TV mode and focus preserved
edge_cases: Back is triggered with Escape or Backspace

journeys.name: Verify the transformation
journeys.outcome: A reviewer can reproduce the app and prove obsolete terminology is absent.

in: Complete TableStory identity and recipe-domain conversion
Mobile browse, search, detail, and My Cookbook

mockups: Mobile recipe detail and saved-state control
TV recipe detail with focusable primary actions
assumptions: The existing Flask application remains the runtime foundation
Saved recipes reset on server restart
